problem.statement: Tensor Core from Volta to Blackwell

payload.title: Tensor Core from Volta to Blackwell
payload.summary: A detailed technical walkthrough of NVIDIA Tensor Core architecture evolution from Volta through Blackwell, covering PTX programming models, each generation's MMA instructions, memory hierarchy changes, and the progression toward fully asynchronous execution.

sections.heading: 1. Performance Engineering First Principles
sections.gist: For a fixed-size problem, Amdahl's Law defines the maximum speedup achievable through parallelization.

sections.heading: 2. PTX Programming Model
sections.gist: Parallel Thread Execution (PTX) is a virtual ISA abstracting GPU generations.

sections.heading: 3. Volta: 1st Generation Tensor Core
sections.gist: GPU instruction dispatch consumes ~30 pJ, while a basic floating-point operation (HFMA) costs only ~1.5 pJ — a 20x overhead ratio.

sections.heading: 4. Turing: 2nd Generation Tensor Core
sections.gist: Enhanced Volta design with INT8 and INT4 precision support.

sections.heading: 5. Ampere: 3rd Generation Tensor Core
sections.gist: Ampere introduced `cp.async` — direct asynchronous GMEM→SMEM copy bypassing registers.

sections.heading: 6. Hopper: 4th Generation Tensor Core
sections.gist: New hierarchy between CTA and grid: clusters correspond to SMs within a GPC.

sections.heading: 7. Blackwell: 5th Generation Tensor Core
sections.gist: New 256 KB per-SM memory (128 lanes × 512 columns × 4 bytes).

sections.heading: 8. Architectural Trends
sections.gist: NVIDIA aggressively scales individual Tensor Core size over core count.
